intro.text: Hi Alex, I'm Remy — your care guide. How are you feeling? Let me have Jack pull your latest records so we're on the same page.

recordsAgent.title: Pulling your latest records
tasks: Checking what your care team handled

summary.text: Okay, Jack's back. In short: you were diagnosed with type 2 diabetes today — your blood sugar's a bit high, but it's very manageable, and your team already handled a few things. What would help most? Ask me anything, or tap a suggestion.

diagnosis.label: What does my diagnosis mean?
diagnosis.userText: What does my diagnosis actually mean?

response.text: Type 2 diabetes just means your blood sugar runs higher than ideal. Your A1c — a three-month average — is 7.8%, and 6.5% or above counts as diabetes, so you're just over the line. It's common, very treatable, and not an emergency.

metformin.label: Do I need metformin?
metformin.userText: Do I really need to take metformin?

response.text: Metformin is the standard first medication — it helps your body use insulin better, it's inexpensive, and most people do fine on it with food. Dr. Lee started you at 500 mg twice a day; it's worth starting, and you can revisit it at your follow-up.

citation.quote: Initiate metformin 500 mg PO BID with meals
citation.label: After-Visit Note

response.text: Three things: pick up your metformin and take it with meals, recheck your A1c in about three months, and get a quick eye screening. Your team already sent the prescription and referral — I can handle the rest whenever you're ready.

pickup.label: Help me get my prescription
pickup.userText: Can you help me get my prescription?

response.text: Your metformin's already waiting at the CVS on Main Street, ready this afternoon.

propose.prompt: Want me to text you directions and a reminder to pick it up?
propose.confirmedText: Done — directions and a 3:30 PM reminder are on your phone.

reminder.label: Set a medication reminder
reminder.userText: Can you remind me to take my medication?

response.text: Taking metformin at the same time each day — with dinner works well — makes it much easier to stay consistent.

propose.prompt: Should I set a gentle daily reminder for 6:30 PM?
propose.confirmedText: Set — I'll remind you at 6:30 PM each day.

response.text: Dr. Lee wants to recheck your A1c in about three months to see how it's trending.

propose.prompt: Want me to find a time with Dr. Lee and add it to your calendar?

card.title: Follow-up booked
card.detail: A1c recheck with Dr. Lee · Sep 14, 10:00 AM

propose.confirmedText: Booked — September 14th at 10 AM with Dr. Lee, on your calendar.

response.text: Diabetes can affect your eyes over time, so a yearly screening is wise — your doctor already placed the referral for you.

propose.prompt: Want me to show in-network eye doctors near you?
propose.confirmedText: Here are three in-network optometrists within four miles — pick whichever's easiest.

peer.label: Connect me with someone like me
peer.userText: Can I talk to someone who's going through this?

response.text: A lot of people feel overwhelmed early on, and hearing from someone who's been there really helps.

propose.prompt: There's a 38-year-old near you who also has type 2 diabetes and chose to be available to support others. Want me to add them to your connections? I only ever show people who opted in.
propose.confirmedText: Added — reach out whenever you're ready, no pressure at all.

records_check.label: Is anything in my records wrong?
records_check.userText: Is everything in my records correct?

response.text: I did spot something — your chart lists a penicillin allergy, and you've mentioned before it isn't actually yours. You have the right to get that corrected.

propose.prompt: Want me to flag it for your care team to review and fix?
propose.confirmedText: Flagged — your care team will review and correct it.

done.label: I'm all set for now
done.userText: I think I'm good for now.

response.text: You did great today, Alex. Everything's in motion, and I'm here whenever you need me. Anything that ever feels serious, reach out to Dr. Lee. Take care.
